grammar.title: 3B: Articles - a / an, the, no article
grammar.explanation:
Use **a** or **an** when you talk about one thing for the first time. We say **a boss** or **an interview** when we say them for the first time.

Use **an** before a vowel sound. Say **an interview**, not a interview.

Also use **a** or **an** to say what something is. For example: **a promotion** is a better job with more pay, and **a deadline** is the last day to finish work.

Use **the** when you both know which one you mean. First you say **a desk**, then you say **the desk** because we know which desk.

Use **the** with the only one, and with superlatives. For example: **the best salary** in the company.

Use **no article** for things in general. Say **customers** are important and **colleagues** are kind when you mean all of them.

Use **no article** after **at**, **to**, and **from** with work, home, and school. Say **I go to work**, and **overtime** is work after hours.

Use **no article** with meals, days, and months. We have **lunch** at noon, and we have a meeting **on Monday**.
examples: I met *a boss* from another office. (first mention)
She is talking to *a colleague*. (first mention)
*A salary* is paid every month. (saying what it is)
I have *an interview* tomorrow. (an before a vowel sound)
I bought a desk. *The desk* is big. (mentioned before)
He got *a promotion* this year. (first mention)
She has *the best salary* in the company. (superlative)
I do not like *overtime*. (general, no article)
*The customer* was happy with our work. (we know which customer)
*The deadline* is Friday. (we know which deadline)
I go *to work* at eight. (no article after to)
We have a meeting *on Monday*. (no article with days)

practice.q: Which is correct: 'a interview' or 'an interview'?
practice.a: 'An interview' — use 'an' before a vowel sound.

practice.q: Which is correct: 'I go to the work' or 'I go to work'?
practice.a: 'I go to work' — no article after 'to' with 'work'.

practice.q: Fill the blank: I saw a customer. ___ customer was happy.
practice.a: The customer was happy — use 'the' when we know which one.
